narrative.overview:
The system behaves like a document a company keeps about itself. The ground is a warm off-white, never a cold white or a neutral grey, so the ink can be a warm near-black and the single accent reads as the same family rather than a second hue.

Structure is drawn, not simulated. No shadow appears anywhere: surfaces separate with a one-pixel rule, stacked panes are offset instead of overlapped, and order is carried by numerals rather than by depth.

One accent marks; it never decorates. It appears on source numbers, entry numbers under the pointer, the waiting state, primary-button hover and focus rings. A colour that is only making the page prettier is wrong.

The marketing surface and the app share the palette and both faces. The display serif crosses into the app exactly once per screen, on the page title, and never touches a label, a control or a value.
keyCharacteristics: One ground, one ink, one accent; state colours are not accents.
Hairlines carry every division. No box-shadow exists in the system.
Ink tints are the same warm black at lower strength, never grey, and never past --ink-subtle.
Composition is asymmetric: the hero headline and its reading copy sit on a diagonal, not a centre line.
One orchestrated load animation per surface, then stillness. Documents do not perform.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every colour in the system is a step on the rust to ember to gold ramp, plus the two semantic signals. There is no blue, no violet, no grey. A proposed colour that cannot be placed on that ramp does not belong to this system.

rules.name: The Tinted Text Rule
rules.body: Secondary and tertiary text is the cream foreground at reduced opacity, never a grey. The alpha floor is .52; below that, 4.5:1 against the ground gives out.

rules.name: The Semantic Distance Rule
rules.body: Only two semantic colours exist, and both are deliberately far enough from the accent that a status pill can never be mistaken for a button.

rules.name: The One Serif Per Screen Rule
rules.body: The display serif appears once on an authenticated screen, as its title. A serif label, a serif button, or a serif value is always wrong.

rules.name: The -0.02em Floor Rule
rules.body: Display tracking never goes tighter than -0.02em. The system previously ran -0.059em at 118px and the letterforms collided.

rules.name: The 13px Floor Rule
rules.body: No real text renders below 0.8125rem. Metadata that will not fit at that size is metadata the screen does not need.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Light Rule
rules.body: A zero-offset coloured shadow is only permitted on an element that is supposed to be emitting light. Everything else uses tone and a hairline. A glowing card is a category error.

rules: Disabled is a colour, not a transparency: fading a control fades its text and its ground together. Disabled primary is rgba(25,20,16,.28) under rgba(250,248,244,.9); every other disabled control keeps its ground and drops its text to --on-night-subtle. Nothing disabled falls below 5:1.
No low-opacity warm radial over a working surface. It reads as haze rather than light, and a contrast checker reading through it reported 2:1 for text that measures 17.7:1.
dos: Do reach for a hairline before a radius, a numeral before an icon, and the spacing scale before a hand-picked value.
Do keep the accent to marks: numbers, states, focus.
Do tint secondary text from the ink, never toward grey, and never past --ink-subtle.
Do offset stacked surfaces rather than overlapping them, so no content is clipped mid-row.
Do give every interactive element hover, focus-visible, active and disabled before shipping it.
Do keep one authored motion moment per surface and use cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) at 200-300ms for everything else.
donts: Don’t add a shadow, a glow or a gradient. If something needs to separate, it gets a rule.
Don’t put an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading. The heading carries its own weight.
Don’t centre a hero block. The asymmetry is the composition.
Don’t introduce a second accent hue.
Don’t number sections unless the sequence itself is information the reader needs. The seven layers are; a three-card row is not.
Don’t build a page out of same-size cards of dot plus heading plus text.
Don’t stand a Unicode glyph in for an icon. Icons are drawn SVG at a single 1.5 stroke.
Don’t use monospace as a costume for technical. It is for keys, commands and code.
Don’t animate padding, width, height or margin. Transform and opacity only.
Don’t let the display serif touch a label, a control, or a value.
